title: Development of a Diagnostic Model for Focal Segmental Glomerulosclerosis: Integrating Machine Learning on Activated Pathways and Clinical Validation
summary: Across 163 patients with focal segmental glomerulosclerosis and 42 living-donor controls in GEO cohorts, the glmBoost+Ridge model using six genes distinguished FSGS from controls. Its AUCs were 1.000, 0.994 and 1.000 across three development/validation cohorts and 0.910 and 0.775 in two platforms of the external cohort (overall AUC about 0.885). Immunohistochemistry supported elevated CD99 and OAZ2 expression. These retrospective expression-cohort results and small tissue validation do not establish clinical diagnostic utility.
organization: The First Affiliated Hospital of Anhui Medical University; The Second People's Hospital of Hefei

evidence.tested: The glmBoost+Ridge six-gene FSGS model was tested across three GEO cohorts and an independent GEO cohort; internal AUCs were 1.000, 0.994 and 1.000, while the external cohort platform AUCs were 0.910 and 0.775 (combined about 0.885). Immunohistochemistry in 16 FSGS patients and 7 controls supported CD99/OAZ2 expression differences.
evidence.unknown: Near-perfect cohort AUCs may not generalize; the independent GEO platform results differed, and clinical diagnostic utility was not demonstrated.
evidence.ai_role: glmBoost+Ridge combines six gene-expression features (BANF1, TUSC2, SMAD3, TGFB1, CD99 and OAZ2) to classify focal segmental glomerulosclerosis.

source_review.scope: Primary result-bearing material for the stated method, result and evaluation, with bibliographic version information.
